title: Nancy Mace criticizes DC diversity programs and reflects on historic graduation from The Citadel
text:
← Back to the wire
Nancy Mace criticizes DC diversity programs and reflects on historic graduation from The Citadel
Rep. Nancy Mace addressed criticism toward D.C.'s diversity offices and recounted her experience as the first woman graduate from The Citadel's Corps of Cadets across three posts dated October 13–14, 2026.
Rep. Nancy Mace, U.S. Congresswoman representing South Carolina’s 1st district since 2021, recently used her social media platform to address topics ranging from diversity initiatives in Washington, D.C., to personal reflections on her education at The Citadel.
On October 13, 2026, Mace posted: "The DC government runs an Office of Racial Equity, a Commission on Reparations, an Office of LGBTQ Affairs, and mandatory DEI training for city employees. At least sixteen DEI offices and commissions in all, paid for by taxpayers. We introduced the No DEI in DC Act to abolish https://t.co/Xrus5P2oVi"
Later that evening on October 14, 2026, she referenced Representative Ilhan Omar in a post stating, "Someone please send Ilhan Omar her own tweet. The one where she said “No one is above the law.” She just found out “no one” includes her. https://t.co/Cxu3za4pIu".
The following day, Mace reflected on her experience as a trailblazer at The Citadel with this message: "Being the first woman to graduate from The Citadel’s Corps of Cadets was no easy feat. Dad said, “Don’t call home if you want to quit. Just put on your shoes and start walking.” The Citadel doesn’t just make you tough. It shows you what you’re made of. We never quit. https://t.co/EYxHyGMahX".
Mace has served in Congress since succeeding Joe Cunningham in 2021 after previously serving in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020. Born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977 and currently residing in Charleston at age 45, she became the first woman to graduate from The Citadel's Corps of Cadets with a BS degree in 1999.
